metadata.title: Municipal Public Space Enforcement Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Explore how public-space enforcement would need to change when a court rejects AI-only evidence, residents prohibit persistent recording, the main cleanup contractor fails, or a major event creates a surge while all three constraints shape the response.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: A fixed camera or sensor detects a possible offence, an AI service ranks the alert, officers review captured media, the platform assembles a legal case and fine, a cleanup task goes to the contracted provider, and dashboards report enforcement and cleanliness outcomes. The design assumes the captured evidence remains lawful and admissible and the assigned service provider remains able to act.
metadata.residualArchitecture: The changed design separates raw observation, detection, human assessment, allegation, evidence item, provenance, capture purpose, privacy transformation, retention rule, legal standard, case decision, cleanup need, task, provider, capacity, handoff, cost, recovery, and visible outcome. This lets the city change evidentiary and privacy rules without losing field coordination, and replace a failed contractor without binding the public incident or case to one supplier.
metadata.note: The stress test is about legitimacy and public service, not merely camera uptime. The explicit change is that detection, legal proof, personal data, enforcement, cleanup work, and provider capacity become independently governed parts of one traceable incident.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: An appellate court rules that AI-selected footage alone cannot support an enforcement penalty
stressors.detection: Court judgment, prosecutor and legal guidance, active and appealed cases, detection model and policy versions, media provenance, officer reviews, procedural templates, evidence gaps, and enforcement outcomes.
stressors.attractor: Cases that looked complete are no longer enforceable because the system cannot show the difference between machine suspicion, verified facts, human observation, and the legal elements of an offence. Continuing automated fines causes appeals and distrust; discarding all alerts removes useful field intelligence.
stressors.businessReaction: Suspend affected automated procedures, find open cases, preserve source evidence, define the new proof standard, require qualified human verification and corroboration, update procedure packs, notify affected people, withdraw or rebuild invalid cases, and keep suitable alerts available for cleanup and hotspot response.
stressors.residue: Separate detection event, model output, source observation, evidence item, provenance, integrity proof, officer observation, corroboration, alleged offence, required legal element, evidentiary rule, case decision, notice, appeal, and outcome. AI can prioritize review but cannot silently become the fact or legal conclusion.

impacts.effect: Enforcement speed remains subordinate to evidence that a court and affected resident can inspect and challenge.
Officers turn an alert into a case by proving each legal element rather than approving an AI conclusion.
Review shows source provenance, model role, human observations, corroboration, legal standard, gaps, and appealability.
Evidence admissibility measures accepted legal proof and provenance, not the confidence of detection.
Adds element-by-element evidence review, human attestation, corroboration, court-rule versioning, rework, and withdrawal.
Makes the boundary between detection, evidence, allegation, human judgment, and legal decision explicit.
Preserves original observations, transformations, access, integrity, custody, annotations, and court use.
Ranks review work with visible reasons but cannot mark an offence as legally proven.
Versions required elements, evidence types, human roles, notices, deadlines, and appeal procedures.
Owns the legal case model with police, courts, privacy, evidence operations, model governance, and field services.
Makes human-verifiable evidence and procedural defensibility central to AI-assisted enforcement comparison.

stressors.name: Residents approve a binding rule that prohibits persistent public-space recording and tracking
stressors.detection: Ballot result or ordinance, allowed public purposes, capture zones and schedules, current devices and models, retention and access records, signage, complaints, privacy assessments, partner exports, and enforcement workflows.
stressors.attractor: The city still must respond to dumping and safety issues, but continuous footage, reusable identity or vehicle traces, broad analytics, and long retention are no longer legitimate. Simply masking a dashboard does not remove collection, linkage, copies, or access in downstream cases and partner systems.
stressors.businessReaction: Stop prohibited collection and reuse, redefine narrow event-triggered purposes, minimize data at the edge, mask irrelevant people and places, prevent identity linkage, shorten retention, delete downstream copies, update signage and assessments, enable independent audit, and offer non-camera reporting paths.
stressors.residue: Separate deployment purpose, legal authority, place, time window, sensing mode, raw capture, edge-derived event, privacy mask, personal identifier, permitted use, recipient, retention schedule, legal hold, deletion proof, signage, complaint, and audit. An event may support cleanup or reviewed enforcement without creating a reusable movement history.

impacts.effect: Visible public-space action continues within limits chosen and understandable by residents.
The city reduces nuisance using narrowly scoped sensing, human reporting, field work, and transparent safeguards.
Deployment cannot activate until purpose, capture mode, masking, access, retention, signage, and audit are approved.
Resident confidence reflects both visible improvement and demonstrated limits on observation and reuse.
Adds event-only collection, edge minimization, non-camera intake, downstream deletion, public safeguards, and audit evidence.
Turns each purpose, capture, transformation, use, sharing, retention, and deletion into a governed step.
Enforces approved spatial, temporal, object, identity, and recipient masking before data leaves the edge.
Calculates retention by purpose and case state and produces deletion evidence across derived copies.
Links authority, necessity, alternatives, safeguards, residual issues, review, and public commitments to deployments.
Owns privacy limits with residents, legal, data protection, field deployment, evidence, police, service, and audit teams.
Makes democratically governed data minimization a differentiator in municipal enforcement infrastructure.

stressors.name: The city's primary cleanup contractor becomes insolvent during a sharp rise in illegal dumping
stressors.detection: Insolvency and contract notices, provider workforce and vehicle availability, open and accepted tasks, site and waste type, legal handling requirements, subcontractors, disposal capacity, invoices, performance bonds, resident complaints, and recurrence signals.
stressors.attractor: Actionable incidents and legal cases continue to arrive, but the provider bound to inspect, remove, transport, document, and invoice the work cannot perform. Reassigning a queue loses accepted-task state, hazardous-waste qualifications, evidence handoff, site history, cost rights, and proof that the public space was restored.
stressors.businessReaction: Suspend unsafe assignments, locate all open sites and provider-held materials, protect hazardous cases, activate alternate public or private capacity, split and reassign unfinished work, preserve evidence and costs, communicate delays, verify cleanup, pursue contractual recovery, and rebalance routes by public impact.
stressors.residue: Separate public incident, cleanup need, service task, work step, required qualification, site access, provider organization, crew, vehicle, disposal destination, acceptance, physical handoff, evidence obligation, completion, invoice, public cost, contractual recovery, and outcome. Unfinished work can move providers without losing the incident or completed steps.

impacts.effect: Cleanliness operations retain control of public outcomes when a contracted delivery organization disappears.
Managers can preserve site context and recompose qualified cleanup capacity around the highest-impact needs.
A task carries required work, qualifications, site and evidence context, accepted steps, current provider capacity, and fallback options.
First-visit success follows the complete need across provider handoffs rather than one contractor work order.
Adds provider capacity, task decomposition, qualification, handoff, alternative sourcing, cost exposure, and recovery.
Coordinates the public need independently from whichever provider performs each work step.
Versions work, provider acceptance, capacity, qualifications, handoffs, completion evidence, and reassignment.
Combines open need, hazard, recurrence, public impact, provider capacity, and field progress spatially.
Separates cleanup cost, provider invoice, fine, recovery right, bond claim, and public expenditure.
Owns continuity with procurement, alternate providers, municipal crews, waste specialists, evidence, finance, and resident support.
Makes provider-independent municipal field response an operations-platform benchmark.

stressors.name: A city festival creates a dumping surge while AI-only penalties are suspended and the cleanup contractor has failed
stressors.detection: Festival zones and schedule, approved event-only sensing purposes, resident and officer reports, AI-ranked alerts, human and corroborating evidence, legal procedure state, cleanup needs and hazards, municipal and alternate-provider capacity, site outcomes, and public communication.
stressors.attractor: The city faces visible nuisance and political pressure but cannot rely on continuous recording, machine-selected footage alone, or its usual service provider. Treating every signal as an offence overwhelms officers; waiting for perfect cases leaves public space unusable and residents uninformed.
stressors.businessReaction: Activate narrowly scoped festival sensing and public reporting, use AI only to prioritize human review, separate cleanup urgency from enforceability, route qualified work across available providers, preserve lawful evidence for selected cases, publish service status and safeguards, and review outcomes after the event.
stressors.residue: No new structural change is required: event-only purpose and deletion controls keep observation proportionate, human-verifiable evidence supports enforceable cases, and provider-independent cleanup tasks restore sites despite contractor failure. One incident view coordinates but does not collapse these decisions.

impacts.effect: The city can respond visibly to an exceptional event without abandoning legal proof or resident privacy limits.
Leadership can explain the service, enforcement, cost, safeguards, and public outcomes of the festival response.
Public reporting separates detections, reviewed incidents, lawful cases, cleanup actions, restored sites, recurrence, and complaints.
Visible action includes lawful enforcement, cleanup without a penalty, communication, and verified restoration.
Composes a bounded event response using existing purpose, evidence, service-capacity, and public-outcome controls.
Publishes understandable results and safeguards from the existing incident, case, task, and outcome records.
Maintains the subset of incidents with sufficient human-verified evidence and procedural readiness.
Shows service and legal outcomes separately with capacity, cost, privacy, complaint, and recurrence context.
Explains temporary sensing, safeguards, reporting channels, cleanup status, enforcement scope, and final results.
Coordinates the bounded event response with residents, police, cleanup, privacy, legal, procurement, field, and communications teams.
Makes proportionate multi-agency event response and public proof a smart-city enforcement benchmark.
